forks.title: The uprising: force or politics?
forks.text: The uprising that began in December 1987 has spread across Gaza and the West Bank. The Defence Minister has ordered large-scale force, including beatings in place of live fire; the foreign minister wants an international conference; the prime minister wants only limited autonomy under Israeli terms. Palestinian civilians and Israeli conscripts alike bear the cost of whichever line is chosen.

cite.quote: State Department spokesman Richard Boucher told reporters: “The use of Israeli helicopter gunships, Palestinian attacks against settlements and motorists, the use of mortars by Palestinians and the targeted killings by the Israeli Defense Force...are producing a new cycle of action or reaction which can become impossible to control.”

lasting.label: Washington's support kept
Attack cells left free to plan
Public anger at perceived passivity
Fewer operations to fund

forks.title: A conference to open talks with Jordan?
forks.text: Foreign Minister Peres has put a US-backed 'document of understanding' to the cabinet: an international conference that would open direct talks with Jordan. Prime Minister Shamir calls the idea a trap and the inner cabinet is split 5-5 along party lines, with Defence Minister Rabin backing Peres. The uprising that starts in December follows history either way.

options.label: Block the conference framework and keep the unity government; pursue only direct talks
options.advocate: Prime Minister Shamir and Industry Minister Sharon

cite.quote: It is an insane and monstrous idea, tantamount to fighting for our national suicide
The national unity government can and must continue to govern.
Industry Minister Ariel Sharon charged that the Peres plan would mean the return of Israel to its pre-1967 borders

options.note: The inner cabinet deadlocked 5-5 along party lines, Shamir refused to resign and the unity government went on without a conference (S5150, S5151).

lasting.label: No territorial concessions on the table
US-backed framework blocked from Jerusalem
Territories budgets and labour markets continue undisturbed
No political horizon offered to Palestinians and Arab citizens

options.label: Approve the document: an international conference as an umbrella for direct talks with Jordan
options.advocate: Foreign Minister Peres and Defence Minister Rabin

cite.quote: Peres says his goal is also direct negotiations but that Jordan needs an international “umbrella” for such talks in order to lend them legitimacy
Defense Minister Yitzhak Rabin, a Peres ally, proposed Sunday night that the government invite Shultz to undertake a shuttle mission

lasting.label: Israel seen leading a US-backed peace initiative
Territorial compromise on the table; security hawks object
Likud and Labor split over the conference
US support for the Jordan track
A political track opens for Palestinians and Arab citizens

options.label: Take the dispute to the voters: leave the unity government and call early elections
options.advocate: Foreign Minister Peres and Defence Minister Rabin

cite.quote: Let’s go to the people and bring about elections.
Foreign Minister Shimon Peres today demanded that Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir resign after the coalition government reached a deadlock on a proposed Middle East peace conference.

lasting.label: The coalition collapses into a long campaign
Land for peace settled at the ballot box, not in the cabinet
Budget decisions delayed by a campaign
A mandate test for the peace camp
Government in campaign mode

forks.title: The 415 deportees in south Lebanon
forks.text: After six soldiers and police were killed in eight days, the government expelled 415 suspected Hamas and Islamic Jihad activists into south Lebanon, where Lebanese troops will not let them in; they are camped in the cold at Marj al-Zuhur. The UN Security Council demands their return and Rabin's cabinet is divided between Rabin and Foreign Minister Peres. The expulsion itself follows history; the question is how Israel answers the pressure.

options.label: Keep the expulsion order but pledge to return all the men by the end of 1993
options.advocate: Prime Minister Rabin

cite.quote: Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin said Israel now will concentrate its efforts on reviving the peace negotiations
following the U.N. Security Council’s acceptance of Jerusalem’s pledge to return all the men by the end of this year

options.note: On 12 February 1993 Israel declared the crisis over after the Security Council accepted its pledge to return all the men by the end of the year; 101 were to return at once (S5154).

lasting.label: Mass expulsion condemned by the UN Security Council
Hamas leaders kept out of the territories for a year
Public backs a tough answer to the killings
Palestinians and Arab citizens see collective punishment

options.label: Keep all 415 out and refuse Red Cross aid through Israeli lines until Lebanon takes responsibility
options.advocate: Interior Minister Deri and Housing Minister Ben-Eliezer

cite.quote: If we give in, that will trigger a slow process of extremely heavy international pressure on Israel to take back (the deportees).

Housing Minister Benjamin Ben-Eliezer, who backed Rabin in the Cabinet meeting, observed that, "The government of Israel has taken a decision, and once we take a decision we are determined not to change it. It is the responsibility of the Lebanese government to let the Red Cross into the camp."
The government of Israel has taken a decision, and once we take a decision we are determined not to change it.

lasting.label: Hamas leadership kept out of the territories
Public rallies behind the firm line
UN and Washington press Israel; the talks are suspended
Washington talks stalled and US goodwill spent
Palestinians and Arab citizens see no relief for the exiles

options.label: Let the Red Cross through at once and bring the deportees home early to restart the Washington talks
options.advocate: Foreign Minister Peres, with Minister Baram

cite.quote: Peres had made it clear this week that the expulsion of the Palestinians, even assuming that all were supporters of the militant Islamic Resistance Movement and Islamic Jihad, did not sit well with him and would likely complicate Arab-Israeli peace negotiations.
I think this was a mistaken decision. We would have only demonstrated our magnanimity.

lasting.label: Israel answers world pressure with a humanitarian gesture
Arab citizens see the expulsions undone
Hamas leaders return to the territories sooner
Right-wing parties and the public angered
Talks resume with US goodwill

forks.title: Oslo II: the interim agreement
forks.text: Rabin and Arafat are finishing an interim agreement: the army leaves Jenin, Tulkarm, Qalqilya, Nablus, Bethlehem and Ramallah and most of about 450 villages, the Palestinians elect a council, and a partial redeployment is planned in Hebron, where about 400 Jews live among 120,000 Palestinians. The Knesset vote is expected to be 61-59: the Likud says it leads back to the 1967 lines, while Meretz says it does not go far enough.

options.label: Sign the interim agreement and put it to the Knesset
options.advocate: Prime Minister Rabin

cite.quote: We can continue to kill and be killed, but we can also try to stop this bloody cycle.
The 61-59 vote that Rabin called a motion of confidence in his center-left coalition government

options.note: Signed in Washington on 28 September 1995; the Knesset ratified it 61-59 on 6 October (S5156).

lasting.label: Interim agreement carried out with US backing
Settler protests and a Knesset divided 61-59
Army out of Palestinian towns; security shared with the Palestinian Authority
Trade and investment in the peace years
Arab citizens see a political track

options.label: Refuse the interim agreement, keep the army in the towns and negotiate again from scratch
options.advocate: Likud leader Netanyahu

cite.quote: we can start from scratch
Netanyahu accused Rabin of lying to the public and “galloping back” to the 1967 borders of Israel

lasting.label: Army stays in West Bank towns
Right-wing camp united behind the opposition line
Israel seen walking back from Oslo
Investors see the peace dividend withdrawn
Palestinians and Arab citizens see the occupation continue

options.label: Sign, and also evacuate the Jewish enclave in central Hebron and aim openly at a Palestinian state
options.advocate: Meretz, Rabin's coalition partner

cite.quote: Rabin’s leftist coalition partners from the Meretz Party, meanwhile, charged that he must go further to seek a Palestinian state and evacuate all 400 Jews from the center of Hebron, a city of 120,000 Palestinians.

lasting.label: Israel seen committing to a Palestinian state
Arab citizens see equal protection in Hebron and a state ahead
Settlers, Likud and part of Labor revolt; the coalition majority is at risk
Army out of Hebron's centre and the towns
Cost of evacuating and rehousing settlers

forks.title: Early elections after Rabin's assassination?
forks.text: Since Rabin's assassination in November, polls show Peres well ahead of Netanyahu (50% to 29%), and Labor is urging him to cash in with an early vote. He is also pursuing a deal with Syria in Maryland, and elections are not due until 29 October. For the first time the prime minister will be elected directly.

options.label: Advance the election to late May
options.advocate: Prime Minister Peres, with Labor chairman Zvilli

cite.quote: I have decided to advance the elections to the earliest date that is possible, according to the law.
Labor Party Chairman Nissim Zvilli, a staunch proponent of early elections

options.note: Peres announced on 11 February 1996 that the vote would be moved to late May; the election was held on 29 May (S5159).

lasting.label: Short, bitter campaign with charges of exploiting the nation's grief
Syrian track suspended during the campaign
A short campaign limits economic uncertainty
Voters, not coalition deals, decide the peace process
A new mandate settles security questions

options.label: Keep the October date and use the months to try for a Syrian agreement
options.advocate: Prime Minister Peres (his position in January 1996)

cite.quote: But he has also said that, for now, he sees no reason to move the elections up.

Publicly, Peres has appeared ambivalent on the issue. He agreed to bring forward Labor's internal primaries to March, a move that prepares the party for early elections. He asked Interior Minister Haim Ramon to speed up the technical process of preparing voter lists, so elections could be held as early as mid-May. But he has also said that, for now, he sees no reason to move the elections up.
I do not feel that the period of restabilization has been completed

lasting.label: Syrian track and US shuttle diplomacy kept alive
More time to heal the rift after the assassination
Labor presses for an early vote while its lead erodes
Two Labor members threaten to vote against any Golan deal
Eight more months of political limbo

forks.title: Har Homa: build now?
forks.text: A month after the Hebron agreement, the ministerial committee on Jerusalem is set to approve the first 2,456 apartments of a planned 6,500-home Jewish neighbourhood at Har Homa (Jabal Abu Ghneim) on Jerusalem's south-eastern edge, together with 3,015 units for Arab residents. Palestinians say it encloses East Jerusalem and warn of a repeat of the September clashes; King Hussein and Washington urge a reversal, while many Israelis, including some in Labor, back the project.

options.label: Approve the first phase of Har Homa alongside 3,015 units for Arab neighbourhoods
options.advocate: Prime Minister Netanyahu

cite.quote: We are asserting our right as the sovereign in Jerusalem to build anywhere the government may decide to build
We will build in all of Jerusalem. We will also build at Har Homa

options.note: The ministerial committee approved the first phase on 26 February 1997 and bulldozers broke ground on 18 March (S5160, S5162).

lasting.label: New Jerusalem housing for families
Likud and much of Labor back building in Jerusalem
Jordan, Washington and the Palestinians protest
Unrest in Jerusalem and the West Bank; redeployments delayed
East Jerusalem's Arabs see the city enclosed

options.label: Hold Har Homa and leave Jerusalem's future to the final-status talks
options.advocate: King Hussein of Jordan and the White House

cite.quote: King Hussein of Jordan, whose country maintains the closest ties of any Arab nation to the Jewish state, sent an envoy to Netanyahu urging him to reverse the decision
further complicates an already complicated situation

lasting.label: Jordan and Washington reward the freeze
East Jerusalem's Arabs see no new enclosure
Calm in Jerusalem; redeployments on schedule
Likud hard-liners and partners accuse Netanyahu of freezing Jerusalem
Jerusalem's housing shortage left unaddressed

forks.title: Barak's coalition: who sits in it?
forks.text: Barak won the 17 May election by a landslide and has until 8 July to form a government. Shas, the Sephardic religious party, grew from 10 to 17 seats and is the third largest, although its leader Aryeh Deri has been convicted of bribery; more than 20,000 e-mails urge 'Just Not Shas'. Likud wants a veto over peace decisions and no Golan withdrawal.

options.label: Build the broadest coalition, including Shas but without Likud
options.advocate: Prime Minister-elect Barak

cite.quote: he has said he wants as broad a coalition as possible to lend credibility to his decisions
Shas must be part of Barak’s government

options.note: Barak's seven-party, 75-seat coalition included Shas, Meretz, the NRP, Yisrael Ba'aliya and the Center Party; Likud stayed out and he was sworn in on 6 July (S5166, S5171).

lasting.label: A 75-seat government able to open Syrian and Palestinian talks
A coalition of rivals; Meretz and secular voters angry over Shas
Ministries and funds for six coalition partners
Shas voters in poorer towns represented in government

options.label: Leave Shas in opposition: a coalition of Labor, Meretz, Yisrael Ba'aliya and the Center
options.advocate: Meretz (leader Yossi Sarid) and the 'Just Not Shas' campaigners

cite.quote: A risk is that the left-wing Meretz Party, one of Barak’s natural allies, has threatened to boycott a government that includes Shas.
“Just Not Shas!” was the message on more than 20,000 e-mails that have flooded into Barak’s Tel Aviv office in recent days

lasting.label: A coalition agreed on religion and state
No sectoral payments to Shas's institutions
A peace-minded government with a clear majority
Shas's mainly Mizrahi voters left outside government
Ethnic and religious tension with Shas in opposition

options.label: Give Likud a Golan guarantee and a veto to form a national-unity government
options.advocate: Ariel Sharon and the Likud

cite.quote: Likud insists that Israel not withdraw from the Golan Heights, and also wanted veto power over Barak’s peacemaking decisions.
Sharon said Barak refused to accept some of Likud's more hard-line positions on security issues.
I regret to say that the partnership we were offered was not true partnership

lasting.label: Likud's security conditions govern the talks
Right and left share one government
No Golan or Lebanon moves; Likud holds a veto over the peace talks
Arab citizens see the peace track frozen
A stable broad government and budgets

forks.title: The Mitchell Report: freeze settlements?
forks.text: The Mitchell committee, set up under the October 2000 Sharm el-Sheikh understandings, urges a ceasefire, a '100 percent effort' by the Palestinian Authority against terrorism and an Israeli freeze on all settlement activity, including 'natural growth'. About 200,000 Israelis live in more than 140 settlements among some 3 million Palestinians; Israel's stated policy is no new settlements but expansion of existing ones.

options.label: Accept the ceasefire steps but reject a freeze: no new settlements, existing ones may grow
options.advocate: Prime Minister Sharon

cite.quote: categorically rejected U.S. and international calls to halt the expansion of Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza Strip
We will not pay protection money.

options.note: On 8 May 2001 Sharon rejected a freeze on settlement expansion, saying existing settlements would grow with their population (S5167).

lasting.label: Settlement housing keeps drawing families
Settlements kept as forward positions
Settler camp and the coalition's right satisfied
Washington and Europe call settlement spending provocative
Extra funds for settlements and their security
Palestinians and Arab citizens see settlement growth continue

options.label: Accept all the Mitchell recommendations, including a freeze on settlement growth
options.advocate: The Mitchell committee (former Senator George Mitchell) and the US administration

cite.quote: The GOI should freeze all settlement activity, including the “natural growth” of existing settlements.
a commission led by former U.S. Sen. George J. Mitchell of Maine said Friday that Israel should freeze settlement construction

lasting.label: Israel seen accepting the independent report
A freeze that Palestinians and Arab citizens can see
Settlement outlays saved and US goodwill
Settlers and the coalition's right wing protest
Fewer new homes in settlements
Settler protests and fewer hilltop positions

forks.title: A referendum on disengagement?
forks.text: The Knesset is voting 67-45 for Sharon's plan to leave 21 Gaza settlements and four in the northern West Bank; the cabinet still has to approve each stage. The National Religious Party and Netanyahu with three Likud ministers demand a national referendum, which Sharon says would delay the plan indefinitely. Sharon's own coalition is splitting.

options.label: Refuse a referendum and widen the coalition with Labor and United Torah Judaism
options.advocate: Prime Minister Sharon

cite.quote: He argues that referendum advocates simply are looking for a way to delay the disengagement plan indefinitely, and accused them of planning a putsch against him.
The prime minister said an alliance was the only way to avoid early national elections, a process that could delay or derail the withdrawal plan.

options.note: Sharon rejected a referendum; the Knesset approved a Likud-Labor-UTJ government on 10 January 2005 by 58 to 56 (S5170).

lasting.label: The withdrawal plan kept on schedule
Likud rebels and settlers denounce a withdrawal imposed without a vote
Subsidies for United Torah Judaism and Labor's budget demands
Police and army tied up by settler protests
The right still disputes the plan's mandate
Stable majority passes the 2005 budget

options.label: Hold a national referendum on disengagement before any evacuation
options.advocate: Netanyahu and the National Religious Party (Zevulun Orlev)

cite.quote: Unless Sharon agrees within 14 days to hold a referendum, he, Livnat, Katz and Naveh will leave the coalition as well.

For four hours before the vote, Netanyahu and three other leading Likud ministers — Limor Livnat, Yisrael Katz and Danny Naveh — closeted themselves in a Jerusalem hotel, working on a proposal to condition their support in Tuesday's Knesset vote on a commitment by Sharon to hold a national referendum on disengagement.
The National Religious Party, which is part of Sharon’s government but which opposes disengagement, served the prime minister with an ultimatum: Hold a referendum or else.

lasting.label: Gaza and northern Samaria garrisons stay while the vote is prepared
A public mandate settles the dispute, whichever way the vote goes
Delay seen as stalling by Washington and the Palestinians
Campaign cost and continued garrisons
Months of campaigning split the country

options.label: Hold out for a secular coalition with Shinui and Labor, without United Torah Judaism and its subsidies
options.advocate: Shinui leader Tommy Lapid

cite.quote: Lapid lashed out at Peres, the Labor chairman, for joining a coalition with a religious party rather than holding out for a secular coalition that would include Shinui.
the prime minister’s allocation of about $65 million in subsidies to be disbursed via a religious political party called United Torah Judaism

lasting.label: No subsidies routed through United Torah Judaism
Fewer sectoral transfers in the budget
A coalition agreed on religion and state

Haredi parties in opposition protest the loss of funding

forks.title: The Shin Bet affair: pardon, prosecution or inquiry?
forks.text: Two Palestinian prisoners captured after the 1984 hijacking of a bus were beaten to death in custody, and senior Shin Bet officers are accused of a cover-up. Attorney General Zamir has ordered a police investigation over the objections of the prime minister and the foreign minister, who fear damage to the security service and exposure of the political leadership. The cabinet must decide how the matter ends.

options.label: Accept the Shin Bet chief's resignation and a presidential pardon for him and three aides; no public trial
options.advocate: Prime Minister Peres and Foreign Minister Shamir, with the inner cabinet

cite.quote: Herzog’s decision, combined with the resignation of Shin Bet chief Avraham Shalom, effectively sidetracked a full-scale public inquiry into the scandal
Government leaders had opposed an official investigation, warning that it would damage the top-secret counterterrorism agency

lasting.label: Counter-terror service left to work undisturbed
Pardon widely seen as a cover-up
Rule-of-law concerns about the security services
Palestinians and Arab citizens see security officers placed above the law

options.note: President Herzog pardoned Shin Bet chief Avraham Shalom and three aides, Shalom resigned, and the inner cabinet approved; criticism and court petitions followed (S5450).

options.label: Let the Attorney General's police investigation go forward, with possible indictments of senior Shin Bet officers
options.advocate: Attorney General Yitzhak Zamir

cite.quote: the search for Zamir’s successor was accelerated only after the attorney general decided to order a police investigation of the security scandal

lasting.label: Security services shown to be bound by law
Public trust in the rule of law
Credit for accountability
Shin Bet leadership in turmoil
Coalition strain as the probe nears the political level

options.label: Order a full judicial commission of inquiry, including into the political level
options.advocate: Minister Ezer Weizman and Energy Minister Moshe Shahal

cite.quote: Ezer Weizman, a minister without portfolio in the current government, said he too would support a full-scale inquiry.

Labor’s Energy Minister Moshe Shahal, who is not a member of the “inner Cabinet” which approved the deal, said he will ask at next Sunday’s meeting of the full Cabinet for a full judicial inquiry into the affair

lasting.label: Palestinians and Arab citizens see an open inquiry

forks.title: After the election: the Law of Return or a unity government?
forks.text: The 1 November election gave neither bloc a majority. The ultra-Orthodox parties will back Likud for a price that includes amending the Law of Return so that only conversions by Orthodox rabbis count; Labor opposes the change, and American Jewish organisations warn of reduced support for Israel. The choice decides who can claim citizenship under the Law of Return and who sits in the government.

options.label: Form a Likud-Labor government and drop the pledge to amend the Law of Return
options.advocate: Prime Minister Shamir, with Labor's Peres and Rabin

cite.quote: Shamir said he could have formed a narrow coalition government with small religious and right-wing parties but preferred to share power with Labor
In the new Likud-Labor agreement, the pledge is dropped in favor of maintaining the status quo

lasting.label: American Jewish leaders and Washington reassured
Converts and non-Orthodox Jews keep their access to the Law of Return
Religious parties feel betrayed
Funds promised to religious parties come under review

options.note: Likud and Labor formed a coalition in December 1988 and the pledge to amend the Law of Return was replaced by the status quo; the measure could still be brought to a vote, but Labor was not obliged to support it (S5454).

options.label: Form a narrow coalition with Shas, Agudat Israel and the NRP and legislate Orthodox-only conversion under the Law of Return
options.advocate: Shas (Rabbi Arye Deri) and Agudat Israel

cite.quote: Besides Shas, Agudat Israel, another ultra-Orthodox party, gave Likud its backing with five seats.
The price that Likud paid the religious parties includes support for a controversial law that would grant Orthodox rabbis authority over Jewish conversions.

lasting.label: Housing and religious-education funds for the religious parties' communities
A right-religious majority holds together
Protests from American Jewish organisations and Washington
Non-Orthodox converts and their families lose automatic eligibility to immigrate
Secular Israelis protest the religious parties' price

forks.title: What to offer Syria on the Golan Heights
forks.text: Secretary of State Christopher is preparing a shuttle between Jerusalem and Damascus. About 16,000 Israelis live in 33 Golan settlements; Syria demands a full withdrawal for normal relations, while hawks in the Labor Party want any significant pullback to need a Knesset super-majority and a national referendum.

options.label: Offer a shallow first pullback, a three-year test of normal relations, then a phased withdrawal
options.advocate: Prime Minister Rabin

cite.quote: Rabin said Israel would then want, as part of that test, a three-year period to develop diplomatic relations and other ties before proceeding with a more substantial but phased withdrawal from the region.

lasting.label: Israel seen as ready to trade land for peace with Syria
The 1994 offer stays on record in later talks
Golan settlers, the right and Labor hawks protest
Security arrangements for a Golan pullback under discussion

options.note: Rabin put the phased offer to Syria in September 1994; Syria's foreign minister criticised the three-year period and the talks produced no treaty (S5456).

options.label: Offer withdrawal to the 1967 line at once in return for full peace
options.advocate: Syrian Foreign Minister Farouk Shareh

cite.quote: Farouk Shareh, Syria’s foreign minister, said in a Dutch television interview rebroadcast in Israel on Thursday evening that his country still wants a full withdrawal

lasting.label: A peace treaty with Syria within reach
US aid and investment for a Syrian peace
Regional trade opens after peace
Golan settlers, the right and Labor hawks rebel
Golan positions given up

options.label: Rule out a significant Golan withdrawal and require 70 Knesset votes and a 65% referendum for any pullback
options.advocate: Labor MK Avigdor Kahalani and seven Labor Knesset members

cite.quote: Avigdor Kahalani, a Labor member of the Knesset, or Parliament, and a retired general who fought in the Golan, warning against any retreat from the territory.

Seven Labor members of the Knesset said they would support legislation requiring 70 of the 120 members of Parliament and then 65% of voters in a national referendum to endorse any significant withdrawal from the Golan

lasting.label: Golan heights kept

Seen as blocking talks with Syria

forks.title: The East Jerusalem land seizure
forks.text: The government has ordered the confiscation of 131 acres in southern Jerusalem, most of it Palestinian-owned, for a police station and Jewish housing, the first such seizure in East Jerusalem since 1981. The Palestinian Authority says the talks are at risk, Arab states have gone to the UN Security Council, and the Arab parties that back the minority government threaten a no-confidence vote. The 1993 accords leave Jerusalem to final-status talks.

options.label: Cancel the confiscation order
options.advocate: Prime Minister Rabin, under pressure from the Meretz ministers and the Arab parties

cite.quote: The four Meretz Cabinet ministers had demanded that the government freeze or cancel its order to confiscate the land
The day after they forced Israel’s government to back down from its plan to confiscate Palestinian-owned property here

lasting.label: Arab citizens see their parties able to affect policy
Talks with the Palestinian Authority protected
Fewer flashpoints in Jerusalem
Right wing accuses the government of weakness
Fewer new apartments in East Jerusalem

options.note: On 22 May 1995, facing a no-confidence motion backed by the Arab parties, the government backed down from the confiscation plan (S5460).

options.label: Carry out the confiscation and promise no further seizures for housing
options.advocate: Foreign Minister Peres

cite.quote: Israeli Foreign Minister Shimon Peres, who has criticized the confiscation plan and complained publicly that it was decided on without any Cabinet discussion, said Sunday that the government cannot back down now.

lasting.label: Housing for families in Jerusalem
Apartments and a police station built
Right wing satisfied
Palestinians and Arab citizens see land taken in East Jerusalem
UN and Arab condemnation; talks at risk

forks.title: Who holds the Gaza-Egypt border?
forks.text: With the withdrawal from Gaza set to start, Egypt has offered to post its own border police along the Philadelphi strip. Defence Minister Mofaz says this does not endanger Israel; Netanyahu says Israel must keep control of the border, the sea and the airspace, and points to smuggling tunnels. The border also governs trade and movement for Gaza's Palestinian residents.

options.label: Withdraw from the Philadelphi strip and let Egyptian border police deploy along the Gaza frontier
options.advocate: Prime Minister Sharon and Defence Minister Mofaz

cite.quote: Defense Minister Shaul Mofaz, a former army chief of staff and a Sharon ally, said, “I want to tell all the members of the house who don’t understand -- reality has changed.” He said the decision to allow Egyptian border police along the eight-mile stretch of desert “does not endanger Israel’s security.

Israel’s parliament Wednesday approved a plan for Egypt to post troops along that country’s border with Gaza, setting the stage for an Israeli military pullout from the coastal frontier it has held for 38 years.

lasting.label: Egypt brought in as a border partner
Egyptian role on the border remembered
No garrison on the border strip
Smuggling tunnels harder to police
Likud rift widens over the withdrawal

options.note: On 31 August 2005 the Knesset voted 53-28 for Egyptian troops on the Gaza border, setting the stage for an Israeli pullout from the strip it had held for 38 years (S5461).

options.label: Keep Israeli control of the Egypt-Gaza border, the Gaza seacoast and airspace
options.advocate: Benjamin Netanyahu

cite.quote: Netanyahu insisted on Israeli control of the Egypt-Gaza border, the Gaza seacoast and airspace.

lasting.label: Tunnel smuggling policed from the border
Likud hard-liners satisfied
Garrisons kept along the border and coast
